about: What Bread Planner shows for each input, recorded from the code before the rebuild and reproduced by every step since. Step 3c left out the hidden manual-rye recipe, which the rebuild does not carry, from the saved-data results. tests/baseline/baseline.test.ts checks the current code against it.

texts: Feed starter
Keep an established starter on its regular feeding routine.
Start leaven
Mix 14 g mature starter, 35.5 g Anita's all-purpose flour, 35.5 g whole-wheat flour and 71 g water. Keep it separate from the autolyse and cover. You use 100 g in the dough and keep 56 g.
Use when aerated and puffy, and a spoonful floats in room-temperature water. If it sinks, allow more fermentation before mixing.
Start autolyse
Mix Anita's all-purpose flour (400 g), whole-wheat flour (50 g), water (340 g). Cover. Keep the remaining ingredients for the final mix.
Mix final dough
Add these after the autolyse. Mix until incorporated.
Start bulk fermentation
Keep covered in a warm place, about 75°F to 80°F / 24°C to 27°C.
Turn 1
With wet hands, stretch and fold all four sides vigorously, then go around a second time. These early turns build the gluten structure.
Turn 2
Vigorously again: stretch and fold all four sides twice, with wet hands.
Turn 3
Turn 4
From here, one round: stretch and fold all four sides once, with wet hands.
Turn 5
Stretch and fold all four sides once, with wet hands.
Turn 6
Turn 7
Cut and preshape
Turn the dough out of its container onto your work surface. Cut it into equal pieces and shape each into a taut round.
Look for a billowy dough and 20% to 30% volume increase.
Bench rest
Cover the rounds. Prepare towel-lined baskets dusted with rice flour.
Final shape
Fold the edges toward the center and roll into a taut round. Place it seam-side up in a prepared basket.
Basket rest
Leave the baskets covered at room temperature.
Overnight cold proof
Cover the shaped loaves in their baskets and refrigerate overnight.
Take the loaf out of the fridge
Allow the loaf to warm while the oven and pots heat.
Preheat oven and Dutch oven
Place the lidded Dutch oven or pots in the oven and heat to 540°F / 282°C. Use one suitable pot per loaf baked at once.
Bake covered
Dust the loaf tops. Carefully turn seam-side down into the hot pot, score with a lame or razor, and cover. Reduce oven to 460°F / 238°C.
Remove lid
Remove lid carefully: hot steam can escape. Continue at 460°F / 238°C.
Bake until the crust is a rich golden brown; extend the uncovered bake if needed.
Loaf out of the oven
Transfer to a wire rack. The base should sound hollow when tapped. Cool each loaf at least 15 minutes before slicing.

Make leaven
Mix 7.5 g (about 1 tbsp) of mature starter with 100 g water, then add 50 g white-bread flour and 50 g whole-wheat flour. Cover at room temperature. You use 100 g in the dough and keep 107.5 g.
Mix dough and rest
Disperse the leaven used in the initial water, about 80°F / 27°C. Add white and whole-wheat flour; mix until no dry flour remains. Cover for 25 to 40 minutes.
Add salt and final water
Work in the salt and reserved water. Keep mixing if the dough separates; it should come together again.
Begin warm bulk fermentation
Cover and keep at 75°F to 80°F / 24°C to 27°C.
Wet your hand. Stretch one quadrant over the dough; rotate and repeat to fold all four sides.
Repeat the four-sided stretch and fold, with wet hands.
Divide and preshape
Dust the top, divide equally and turn flour-side down. Shape taut rounds with the dusting flour on the outside.
Look for a billowy dough and 20% to 30% volume increase. The book allows up to one more hour with folds if needed; wait until the dough is ready before moving on.
Bench rest and prepare baskets
Cover the rounds for 30 minutes. Line proofing baskets or bowls with towels and generously dust with rice flour.
Turn flour-side down. Stretch and fold the bottom, sides and top over the center; roll seam-side down into a taut round. Place seam-side up in a prepared basket.
Refrigerated final proof
Cover the baskets and refrigerate for 10 to 12 hours.
Warm the loaf to room temperature
Remove the loaf from the refrigerator.
Bring the dough back to room temperature before baking; use its condition, rather than the clock alone.
Place the lidded Dutch oven or pots in the oven and heat to 500°F / 260°C. Use one suitable pot per loaf baked at once.

Cover and keep at 75°F to 80°F / 24°C to 27°C for 3 to 4 hours.

Mix 22.5 g (about 1 tbsp) of mature starter with 300 g water, then add 150 g white-bread flour and 150 g whole-wheat flour. Cover at room temperature. You use 300 g in the dough and keep 322.5 g. Each of the 2 bowls gets 150 g.

Split this mix between 2 bowls, with an equal share of everything in each. Disperse the leaven used in the initial water, about 80°F / 27°C. Add white and whole-wheat flour; mix until no dry flour remains. Cover for 25 to 40 minutes.
Work the salt and reserved water into each bowl. Keep mixing if the dough separates; it should come together again.
Combine both bowls in one container. Cover and keep at 75°F to 80°F / 24°C to 27°C.
Add the olive mixture

In a bowl, stir together 1½ cups pitted olives, coarsely chopped; 1 cup toasted walnuts or hazelnuts, coarsely chopped (optional); 1 teaspoon dried herbes de Provence; grated zest of ½ lemon. Scatter the mixture over the dough, add a splash of water, and work it in by hand, cutting through and folding the dough until it is evenly spread. Then carry on with bulk as planned.

In a bowl, stir together 3 cups pitted olives, coarsely chopped; 2 cups toasted walnuts or hazelnuts, coarsely chopped (optional); 2 teaspoons dried herbes de Provence; grated zest of 1 lemon. Scatter the mixture over the dough, add a splash of water, and work it in by hand, cutting through and folding the dough until it is evenly spread. Then carry on with bulk as planned.

In a bowl, stir together 4½ cups pitted olives, coarsely chopped; 3 cups toasted walnuts or hazelnuts, coarsely chopped (optional); 3 teaspoons dried herbes de Provence; grated zest of 1½ lemons. Scatter the mixture over the dough, add a splash of water, and work it in by hand, cutting through and folding the dough until it is evenly spread. Then carry on with bulk as planned.
Toast the sesame seeds

Heat the oven to 400°F / 204°C. Give the seeds 10 minutes on a rimmed baking sheet in a single layer, then stir them so the darker ones at the edges move to the middle. Return them for another 10 to 15 minutes, until thoroughly toasted, and let them cool for 20 minutes. They go into the dough at Turn 1.
Add the toasted sesame seeds

Scatter over the dough ½ cup unhulled sesame seeds, toasted and cooled. Wet them with a splash of water, then work them in by hand, pinching the dough through your fingers and slicing through it with the side of your hand until the seeds are evenly spread. Bulk then carries on as planned.

Scatter over the dough 1 cup unhulled sesame seeds, toasted and cooled. Wet them with a splash of water, then work them in by hand, pinching the dough through your fingers and slicing through it with the side of your hand until the seeds are evenly spread. Bulk then carries on as planned.
